senses.gloss:
Buḍila Āśvatarāśvi or āśvatara āśvi is mentioned several times in the brāhmaṇa literature as a teacher. According to the Chāndogya and the Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣads, he was a contemporary of janaka of videha, and, according to the Śatapatha brāhmaṇa, of aśvapati, the kekaya king. He is also mentioned in the aitareya brāhmaṇa.^4
